digest.top_line: RTOG 0848: adjuvant chemoRT after gemcitabine misses OS (HR 0.96), but node-negative pts gained OS (interaction P=.0063).
digest.tldr: Hepatobiliary carried the day's only signal: RTOG 0848 puts 50.4 Gy/28 fx with modern IMRT + central QA on trial and finds no OS benefit overall, but a node-status interaction (OS P=.0063, DFS P=.014) favoring CXRT in N0. Hypothesis-generating in 91 pts, not a mandate.

sites.intro: First contemporary-technique test of adjuvant pancreatic CXRT since ESPAC-1; the RT question narrows to N0 disease.

studies.name: RTOG 0848
studies.tldr: OS HR 0.96 (90% CI 0.79-1.18), 1° EP not met; node-negative subgroup gained OS (interaction P=.0063).
details: 📊 1° EP OS not met: HR 0.96 (90% CI, 0.79 to 1.18), one-sided P=.38, two-sided P=.77
📐 DFS trend only: HR 0.82 (95% CI, 0.65 to 1.03), P=.089
📊 Treatment × nodal status interaction: OS P=.0063, DFS P=.014, favoring CXRT in N0
🔍 Step 2 randomization only after 5 cycles chemo without progression, enriching out early systemic failure
🔍 RT: 50.4 Gy/28 fx to tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy, regional nodes; 81% IMRT, real-time central QA review
💊 Sensitization capecitabine 83%, infusional 5-FU 15%; step 1 was gemcitabine ± erlotinib, zero FOLFIRINOX
📊 G3 AEs 38% v 19% (P<.001), mainly GI/diarrhea and lymphopenia; G4/5 unchanged (6% v 5%, P=.68)
⚠️ 14% assigned to CXRT never got it (18 refusals); as-treated sensitivity HR 0.98 (90% CI, 0.80 to 1.20)
⚠️ Node-negative signal is a subgroup of 91 pts with wide CIs; N0 forest interaction P=.022 while global claim rests on multivariable interaction
⚠️ Accrual took ~9 years; final analysis triggered at 270 OS events (power 72%), not the planned 316
🔗 vs ESPAC-1, where CXRT was detrimental: that trial used split-course, lower-dose 2D RT (1994-2000) with no QA and no postop imaging to exclude early mets

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase III, prespecified OS primary not met, so adjuvant CXRT is not supported broadly; the N0 benefit rests on a subgroup interaction, not a powered comparison.
verdict.audience: Resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma, R0/R1, post 5 cycles gemcitabine-based adjuvant chemo

studies.significance: The RT read is the nodal interaction: in N0 pts (n=91), median OS 3.9 vs 3.0 yr and 5-yr OS 48.1% vs 28.6% with CXRT, delivered as 50.4 Gy/28 fx to bed, pancreatojejunostomy and regional nodes with real-time central QA. That is the population and the technique worth carrying into a trial, not into routine adjuvant practice.
studies.monday_clinic: In resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma with pathologically negative nodes who completed adjuvant chemo without progression, this supplies the strongest randomized signal yet for adding CXRT, though as a subgroup finding; it does not extend to node-positive pts, where no treatment effect was seen.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: 90% CI 0.79-1.18, one-sided P=.38; primary end point not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter randomized **phase IIR/III**, two-step. Step 1 gemcitabine ± erlotinib (reported previously); **step 2** randomized 1:1 to a sixth chemo cycle ± CXRT among pts without progression after five cycles. Opened 2009, step 2 closed 2018, analyzed December 2023; median follow-up 2.2 yr overall, **7.4 yr in survivors**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Curative-intent resection of **pancreatic head** adenocarcinoma with gross total resection on the operative note and documented microscopic margin status; body/tail excluded on the basis of RTOG 9704. N=354 (174 chemo, 180 chemo+CXRT), median age 63, **74% node-positive**, 81% pT3, 17% margin-positive, 96% postop CA19-9 ≤90.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50.4 Gy/28 fx** starting within 21 days of cycle 6, covering tumor bed, pancreatojejunostomy and regional nodes; 81% IMRT, 19% 3D conformal, centers IROC-credentialed with **real-time central review** before start. Median delivered dose 50.4 Gy over 38 days, 88% received ≥50 Gy, 79% had no interruptions; overall QA per protocol/acceptable in 92% of treated pts.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Sensitization was **capecitabine in 83%** and infusional 5-FU in 15%, two pts received none. Discontinuation for toxicity was 5% with capecitabine and 17% with 5-FU. Adjuvant systemic therapy was gemcitabine (67%) or gemcitabine + erlotinib (28%); **no pt received FOLFIRINOX**.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: OS **HR 0.96** with median 2.6 vs 2.3 yr and 5-yr 23.1% vs 27.9%; DFS **HR 0.82** (P=.089), median 1.0 vs 1.3 yr. Multivariable analysis showed **treatment by nodal status interaction** for OS (P=.0063) and DFS (P=.014), with benefit confined to N0.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No excess grade 4/5 (**6% v 5%, P=.68**), one grade 5 per arm (hepatic failure, sepsis). Grade 3 rose to **38% v 19%** (P<.001), driven by GI toxicity (any G3-5 GI 11% v 2%; diarrhea 6% v 1%) and lymphocyte count decreased (10% v 2%). Nonhematologic G3 22% v 11% (P=.004).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: ESPAC-1 found adjuvant chemoradiation detrimental and effectively ended its routine use outside the US, but used split-course lower-dose 2D RT accrued 1994-2000 without QA or postoperative imaging to exclude early metastatic disease. RTOG 9704's post hoc analysis linked deviation from protocol RT planning to worse survival, which is the specific failure mode 0848's mandatory pre-treatment central review was built to remove.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents resected pancreatic head adenocarcinoma completing gemcitabine-based adjuvant chemotherapy without progression. Does not represent body/tail primaries, FOLFIRINOX-treated pts, or the neoadjuvant setting where nodal status after systemic therapy carries a different meaning.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The comparator backbone is obsolete: gemcitabine ± erlotinib, with **zero FOLFIRINOX**, so whether local therapy still adds anything on a more effective systemic regimen is untested. Only 10 pts total were both node-negative and margin-positive, so the margin question cannot be addressed at all, and the N0 arms carry 42 and 49 pts with medians whose upper CI is not reached.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial's own explanation for the interaction is competing risk: node positivity marks pts who will fail distantly, where better local control cannot show up in OS. That is biologically coherent and consistent with the codominant locoregional/systemic failure pattern, but it is a hypothesis this trial generated rather than tested.

studies.interpretation:
The honest headline is that a randomized phase III asked whether adjuvant chemoradiation adds survival after resection of pancreatic head cancer and answered no, with an HR of 0.96 that sits almost exactly on unity. The authors argue the reduced power (72% at 270 events rather than the planned 316) does not hide a true benefit, and on this point they are right: the observed estimate is nowhere near the hypothesized 0.76, and a wider confidence interval around 0.96 does not rescue a signal that is absent. So the primary reading is settled. Adjuvant CXRT delivered to an unselected resected population does not extend survival.

What makes the trial worth an RT reader's time is the nodal interaction, and how much weight it deserves depends on how one treats a subgroup claim. The usual reasons to discount one apply only partly here. Nodal status was a stratification factor at randomization, not something dredged after the fact, and the interaction was tested in the prespecified multivariable model rather than found by scanning the forest plot. Against that, the node-negative stratum holds 91 pts, the OS interaction P of .0063 in the multivariable analysis is considerably stronger than the .022 the univariable forest reports for the same variable, and the CXRT arm's median OS upper bound is not reached. A 5-year OS of 48.1% versus 28.6% is a very large absolute separation to attribute to 91 pts, and effects estimated in small strata are systematically inflated. The direction is credible; the magnitude almost certainly is not.

The mechanistic argument for the interaction is the strongest thing in the paper. If node positivity marks a population whose dominant risk is distant failure, then improving locoregional control there cannot move OS regardless of how good the radiation is, and any benefit will concentrate where the competing risk is lowest. That prediction was made in advance and matches what the data show. It also explains why the DFS signal for the whole cohort (HR 0.82) points in the right direction while OS does not, and it fits the codominant failure pattern reported in autopsy series. But this reasoning is a hypothesis the trial generated, not one it tested, and it should be treated accordingly.

The more serious problem for transferring any of this is the backbone. Not a single patient received FOLFIRINOX, and by the design's own logic more effective systemic therapy raises rather than lowers the value of local control, since it shifts the competing risk. That cuts both ways: it may mean the node-negative benefit understates what modern sequencing would show, or it may mean the population that stays free of distant disease long enough to benefit looks entirely different. Neither can be resolved here. Similarly, the trial's suggestion that node-negative pts after neoadjuvant chemotherapy are the natural population for the next study collides with the fact that post-neoadjuvant nodal status carries different information than it does after upfront resection.

What the trial does settle, cleanly, is safety. With centrally reviewed, credentialed, mostly IMRT delivery, adding CXRT produced no excess grade 4 or 5 toxicity and a grade 3 increase driven by diarrhea and lymphopenia. Whatever remains of the post-ESPAC-1 concern that adjuvant radiation actively harms these pts does not survive this dataset. The open question is now efficacy on a modern regimen, not tolerability.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The nodal interaction is the RT-relevant result: in N0 pts, median OS 3.9 vs 3.0 yr and 5-yr OS 48.1% vs 28.6%. Technique transfers directly, 50.4 Gy/28 fx to bed, pancreatojejunostomy and regional nodes, 81% IMRT under real-time central review, with no excess G4/5.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The systemic backbone was gemcitabine ± erlotinib with zero FOLFIRINOX, so this does not test whether local therapy adds anything to a modern regimen. For sequencing decisions, the practical read is that CXRT costs G3 toxicity (38% v 19%) without an OS return outside the node-negative stratum.

papers.title: Adjuvant Chemotherapy ± Chemoradiotherapy for Adenocarcinoma of the Pancreatic Head: Results of the Radiotherapy Random Assignment of NRG Oncology/RTOG 0848
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To assess whether adding fluoropyrimidine sensitized radiotherapy (CXRT) to adjuvant chemotherapy improves overall survival (OS) after curative intent resection of the pancreatic head. METHODS This was a multicenter, randomized phase III, two step trial. Step 1: gemcitabine versus gemcitabine + erlotinib (previously reported). Step 2: random assignment to sixth chemotherapy cycle ± CXRT after five cycles of step 1 chemotherapy without progression. Outcomes of step 2 random assignment are reported here. Assuming 17 months median OS (chemotherapy alone), the sample size was 354 patients (hazard ratio [HR], 0.76, 80% power, one-sided α = .05, 316 OS events). OS/disease-free survival (DFS) were estimated by Kaplan-Meier and arms compared using the log-rank test. RESULTS A total of 354 patients (median age 63, 55% male, 56% performance status, 1) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy (174) or chemotherapy + CXRT (180). Univariable median and 5-year OS (90% CIs) were 2.6 years (2.1-3.1) and 23.1% (17.7-28.6) for chemotherapy alone, and 2.3 years (2.0-2.6) and 27.9% (22.2-33.6) for chemotherapy + CXRT. The OS primary end point was not met (HR, 0.96 [90% CI, 0.79 to 1.18]; one-sided P = .38, two-sided P = .77). Chemotherapy + CXRT was associated with a trend for improved DFS (univariably; HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.65 to 1.03]; P = .089), without increase in grade 4/5 toxicities. However, grade 3 toxicity increased (38% v 19%, P < .001). Significantly, treatment by nodal status interactions showed that CXRT improved OS ( P = .0063) and DFS ( P = .014) in node-negative patients. CONCLUSION Overall, the addition of adjuvant CXRT to adjuvant gemcitabine did not statistically significantly improve OS, DFS, or increase grade 4/5 toxicity. For node-negative patients, CXRT improved OS and DFS. These results, if confirmed in studies with current or future systemic therapies, would support the use of adjuvant/neoadjuvant CXRT for node-negative patients.
